claims.text: Nearly equiatomic AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles are high-entropy alloy nanoparticles.
The AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles have a defined atomic ordering at room temperature.
In-situ high-resolution aberration-corrected TEM with an integrated heating stage can reveal atomic-scale phase transformations and rearrangements during heating.
The proposed in-situ TEM observations would directly validate enhanced thermal stability in AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles.
Controlled high-temperature ramps can be applied through an integrated TEM heating stage while atomic-resolution imaging is performed.
Static isothermal and dynamic temperature-ramp imaging regimes are relevant to the intended high-temperature applications.
Heating produces atomic-level rearrangements and phase-transformation events in the nanoparticles.
Thermal activation promotes atomic diffusion in AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles.
Thermally activated diffusion causes phase reordering and structural evolution.
In-situ TEM can capture thermally driven transformations as they occur.
Atomic-scale phase transitions or reordering events will occur at specific temperature thresholds.
Observing phase transitions or reordering events would support enhanced thermal stability.
TEM resolution may be degraded or limiting at extreme temperatures.
Electron-beam exposure may influence the nanoparticle transformations being measured.
Very rapid structural transitions may not be captured by the imaging method.
A room-temperature sample provides a control for the initial atomic arrangement before thermal exposure.
Failure to observe atomic-scale changes over the expected high-temperature regime would falsify the proposed validation of enhanced thermal stability.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis treats observable transformations as validation of enhanced thermal stability, while the falsification rule treats the absence of transformations as falsifying stability. Structural invariance during heating could instead be evidence for stability, so the proposed observations do not decisively distinguish enhanced stability from instability.
